prompt: Construct a GreenCycle Operations & Content Portal supporting municipal sustainability teams and environmental service providers with a single offline-ready workspace for publishing local guidance and running field operations. Roles include Administrator (system configuration and access), Editor (creates and updates environmental news/policy/education content), Reviewer (approves and schedules releases), Dispatcher (builds schedules and manages changes), and Analyst (reads KPI dashboards and exports reports). The UI is built with Flask-rendered pages enhanced by HTMX for fast in-place updates (inline validation, modal edit forms, and near-instant filter refresh without full page reloads). Editors work in a rich-text CMS flow that supports draft, review, publish, scheduled publish, and withdraw states, plus category/tag taxonomy and pin/recommend/carousel placements for the homepage. Users find content and operational records through on-site full-text search across titles, body, tags, and metadata, with faceted filters by category, date range (MM/DD/YYYY), region, and media type; the system highlights trending search terms and flags “zero-result” queries for content gap review. Dispatchers use an interactive scheduling screen to model classrooms/instructors/time slots as reusable resources, run automatic or semi-automatic scheduling, and visually resolve conflicts (double-booked instructor, overlapping room usage, or time-slot violations) with reschedule/substitute workflows and clear on-screen change notices. Analysts access configurable KPI reporting with turnaround time, on-time rate, exception rate, and cost/revenue views, with multi-dimensional filters, CSV export, and role-based access to sensitive financial fields. On the system side, the backend uses Flask to implement a decoupled REST-style API consumed by HTMX requests, while SQLite persists users, roles, CMS content versions, taxonomy, search indexes, resources, schedules, order lifecycles, and analytics snapshots. Authentication is strictly local username/password with salted hashing; accounts lock for 15 minutes after 5 failed attempts, and session idle timeout is 30 minutes. The service catalog supports hourly, per-use, and package items; orders follow a state machine (created, paid, canceled, completed, refunded) but “paid” is recorded via offline tender types (cash, check, invoice) with an internal receipt number, optional sales-tax rate per region, and reconciliation that flags mismatches over $5.00 for review. Reporting supports pagination by default (50 rows/page), server-side caching of common aggregates for 10 minutes, and asynchronous report generation for queries expected to exceed 5 seconds, providing a downloadable result once complete. File governance enforces a whitelist (PDF, JPG/PNG, DOCX) with a 20 MB limit, blocks executable formats, validates MIME/extension consistency, computes SHA-256 fingerprints to detect duplicate uploads, applies optional visible watermarks on download, and requires signed, time-limited download URLs (10 minutes) with permission checks; all attachments are stored on local disk under a non-public directory with lifecycle rules (archive after 180 days, purge after 7 years if configured). “Open APIs and integrations” are delivered as local-only REST/GraphQL endpoints with JWT access control, API quotas (1,000 requests/day per key), and webhook-style event delivery implemented as an internal outbox/queue for offline consumers; external internet integrations are disabled by default and must remain optional so the system remains fully functional without any network dependency.gurations, all exposed via RESTful APIs that the Angular frontend calls over the local network without any external dependencies. Sensitive fields (addresses, device identifiers, credit history) are encrypted at rest, and screens mask data by role to minimize unnecessary exposure.
